title: An alignment guide counts items the way a person would
goal: A guide's row says how many things it checked, like Left edges, 3 items, but the count comes from runs of ink, not from elements. One label can count twice when a gap splits it, and two things stacked close together can count once. A spec that says 3 items when a designer sees 2 loses trust. The count should match what a person would count, or say something honest when it cannot.
notes: Evidence: audits 2026-09-02-alignment-guide-row (rough 3: items counts runs, a split label counts twice, stacked elements can merge), 2026-09-02-guide-edge-chip (rough 3: 4 items for two buttons) and 2026-09-02-guide-buttons-aligned (border flanks fixed one cause; rough 2 leaves the x-height case). AlignmentScan in PhotonzCore owns the runs. Filed by the 2026-09-02 digest design review.
acceptance: On the settings-pane fixture, a guide across two buttons reads 2 items and a guide down a column of four single-line labels reads 4 items, pinned by tests.
A label the scan splits into two runs counts once; two stacked elements with a visible gap between them count twice.
Where the scan genuinely cannot tell, the row drops the count rather than printing a wrong one.
Scripts/test.sh green; audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task.
